answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with slow-accruing, decaying trust: every new identity starts as a mere ember, able to do only tiny low-value jobs. Trust grows like a glacier, gradually, through months of verified useful work, and when one agent vouches for another, that trust ripples outward but loses strength with each hop, so a cluster of fake identities cannot inflate each other. An attacker would need to sustain thousands of convincing work histories for months, costing far more time and compute than the fraud could repay.
